models.name: Whisper large-v3
models.specialization: Still the safest all-rounder for general transcription. Broad language coverage makes it the default when the input language is unknown.

models.name: Qwen3-ASR
models.specialization: Covers 52 languages and dialects, handling language identification, recognition and timestamp prediction in one model. A good fit for subtitling and anything else that needs timings.

models.name: NVIDIA Canary-Qwen 2.5B
models.specialization: Currently the most accurate option for English. Beats Whisper on English-only workloads.

models.name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT
models.specialization: The fastest self-hostable option for batch throughput. Pick it when transcribing a large archive in one pass.

models.name: Moonshine
models.specialization: Built for real-time recognition on constrained hardware. At 27MB the smallest model fits where Whisper and the NVIDIA models simply cannot run.

models.name: Qwen3-Embedding-8B
models.specialization: Covers 100+ natural and programming languages and leads the MTEB snapshot. Accepts user-defined instructions so behaviour can be tuned per domain. 0.6B and 4B variants let you trade quality for resources.

models.name: BGE-M3
models.specialization: The self-hosted multilingual standard across 100+ languages. The default alternative to Qwen3 where a larger model is impractical to serve.

models.name: BGE-reranker-v2
models.specialization: Reranks embedding search results. Paired with BGE-M3 it completes a two-stage retrieval pipeline at zero licensing cost.

models.name: Qwen3-VL-Embedding
models.specialization: Places text and images in one vector space, so you can retrieve documents by image or images by text. A matching reranker ships alongside it.

models.name: FLUX.2
models.license_note: Licensing differs per variant (dev, schnell, ...) — check each one
models.specialization: Leads open models on photorealism and output quality. Pick it when the result has to stand up as professional work.

models.name: Stable Diffusion 3.5
models.license_note: Free below an annual-revenue threshold; a commercial license is required above it
models.specialization: Deepest ecosystem and the most flexible for fine-tuning. LoRA, ControlNet and the rest of the tooling are richest here, which matters when heavy customization is the point.

models.name: Z-Image Turbo
models.specialization: Matches or beats FLUX.2 [dev], HunyuanImage 3.0 and Imagen 4 while needing only a few inference steps. Useful when latency matters in a composed pipeline.

models.name: Qwen-Image
models.specialization: An image model that is unrestricted for commercial use, and reported to render text inside images unusually well.

models.name: Kimi K3
models.params_note: MoE — all experts must be resident; 104B active per token
models.specialization: Strong on agentic and terminal work. Among the top open-weight models as of its July 2026 release.

models.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
models.params_note: MoE — all experts must be resident; 8B/16B active per token
models.specialization: MoE design keeps active parameters small, so inference is cheap for its size. MIT licensed, so commercial use is unrestricted.

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.license_note: License changed relative to 5.2 — verify the text directly
models.specialization: Frontier-class open-weight model, near the top on aggregate benchmarks.

models.name: GLM-5.3-Flash
models.license_note: Plain MIT, unlike the larger GLM-5.3
models.params_note: MoE — all experts must be resident; 18B active per token
models.specialization: The most permissively licensed model in the GLM-5.3 family. 18B active parameters keep inference cost low.

models.name: Qwen3.6-27B
models.license_note: Qwen models are generally Apache-2.0; confirm per model
models.specialization: A dense 27B that fits on one GPU yet approaches frontier-class coding scores. Best performance-per-host in the self-hosted range.

models.name: Qwen3.8 Max
models.specialization: Ranked first on the September 2026 open-weight leaderboard.

models.name: Qwen3.8-27B
models.specialization: Runs on a single 24GB GPU or a 32GB Mac. The safest default when local execution is a requirement.

models.name: Gemma 4
models.license_note: Google Gemma Terms of Use apply; check the prohibited-use clauses
models.specialization: Among the strongest small models that fit under 16GB. The default pick for laptops and low-end GPUs when everything must run locally.

models.name: Kokoro
models.specialization: Very light at 82M parameters, fast enough on CPU to be the easiest final stage in a local pipeline. It cannot clone a voice from a sample, however.

models.name: F5-TTS
models.license_note: Code is MIT; check separately for constraints tied to training data provenance
models.specialization: Flow-matching based, with notably good voice cloning — give it a reference clip and it synthesizes in that voice. Start here when quality matters most.

models.name: XTTS-v2
models.license_note: Non-commercial use only. It is the most-downloaded TTS model on Hugging Face, but shipping it in a commercial product means ripping it back out later.
models.specialization: Clones a voice into another language from a six-second sample. Capable, but the license rules out commercial use.

models.name: Qwen3-TTS
models.specialization: One of the safe picks for commercial deployment, and easy to pair with other models in the Qwen ecosystem.

models.name: Chatterbox
models.specialization: Safe for commercial deployment and still supports voice cloning — the usual license-safe alternative to XTTS-v2.

models.name: Wan 2.2
models.specialization: Apache-2.0, so commercial use is unrestricted, and the 5B GGUF runs in 8GB of VRAM with memory offloading. The most practical choice when local execution is required. Motion realism and prompt adherence approach Sora and Veo.

models.name: LTX-2.3
models.specialization: The only open model with native audio: it generates synchronized sound and video in a single diffusion pass, at up to 4K and 50fps. No separate audio step means a shorter composed pipeline.

models.name: HunyuanVideo 1.5
models.specialization: Runs on a single RTX 4090 at roughly 14GB of VRAM with FP8 and CPU offloading. A candidate when one consumer GPU is the whole budget.

models.name: CogVideoX
models.specialization: Released early enough to have accumulated tooling and examples — helpful when fine-tuning references are needed.

models.name: Mochi 1
models.specialization: An Apache-2.0 video model, reported to be strong on motion.

models.name: RF-DETR
models.specialization: Tops both COCO and the real-world RF100-VL benchmark. The recommended accuracy-first starting point for most vision projects.

models.name: YOLO26
models.license_note: AGPL-3.0 — a separate commercial license is required for closed-source distribution
models.specialization: Optimized for edge and real-time use. NMS-free end-to-end prediction simplifies post-processing, and CPU inference is up to 43% faster than YOLO11-N. One model covers detection, segmentation, classification, pose and oriented boxes.

models.name: SAM 3
models.specialization: Supports both promptable and open-vocabulary segmentation. Especially useful for building labelled datasets quickly.

models.name: SAM 2
models.specialization: Carries memory across video frames, so an object picked by click, box or mask is tracked to the end of the clip. The first stop for video segmentation.

models.name: GLM-OCR
models.specialization: Extracts text from document images. Among the leading OCR options as of 2026.

models.name: Florence-2
models.specialization: Handles OCR and vision-language tasks in one model. Captioning, detection and OCR are switched by prompt, which makes it easy to drop into a composed pipeline.

models.name: Qwen3-VL
models.license_note: Confirm the license per model size
models.specialization: Front of the pack on both quality and latency among 2026 open VLMs. Used for image description, document understanding and visual agents alike — the default first block in a composed pipeline.

models.name: GLM-4.5V
models.specialization: Strong 3D reasoning. Reported state of the art among similarly sized open models across 42 public benchmarks.

models.name: InternVL3.5
models.specialization: A visual-resolution router improves inference efficiency. The 241B flagship is state of the art among open VLMs.

models.name: Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct
models.specialization: Particularly well suited to visual agents — driving a UI, navigating documents, and other tasks where the model looks at an image and decides what to do next.
